Replaced the 1792 militia system. It divided the militia into an organized part, the National Guard, and an unorganized reserve, and gave the Guard federal funding and equipment in exchange for meeting Army standards.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 32 Stat. 775](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/32/775){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 32 U.S.C. 101 et seq.](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/32/101?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Recognized the National Guard as the organized militia of the states.
- Federal arms, funding, and inspection in return for conformity with Regular Army organization and training.
- Limited federal call-ups in time and, as first interpreted, to service inside the United States.

## Why it matters

It created the National Guard as an institution. The limits on overseas service were removed by the [National Defense Act (1916)](national-defense-act-1916.qmd), and the dual state and federal character it began is the root of [Title 32](title32-usc.qmd).

## Current status

Carried forward by the National Defense Act of 1916 and now reflected in Titles 10 and 32.

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}
